holidays.name: National Wear Your Pearls Day
holidays.description: A day for taking your pearls out of the jewelry box and wearing them. Dress them up with a gown or dress them down with a T-shirt and jeans. Pearls go with everything, so no occasion is required.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular excuse to wear heirloom and everyday pearls.
holidays.funFact: Pearls are one of the few gems made by a living creature. They form inside oysters and mollusks, which layer shimmering nacre around an irritant.

holidays.name: National Cupcake Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the single-serving cake. Bake a batch, buy one from a bakery, or swirl the frosting on extra high. Sprinkles are strongly encouraged.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It is popular with bakeries and sweet tooths in the middle of the holiday baking season.
holidays.funFact: The first known mention of a cupcake appeared in an 1828 cookbook by Eliza Leslie. The name may come from the cups the cakes were baked in, or from recipes that measured ingredients by the cupful.

holidays.name: National Gingerbread Latte Day
holidays.description: A toast to the coffee drink that tastes like a gingerbread cookie. It's a mix of espresso, steamed milk, and warm spices like ginger, cinnamon, and molasses. Make one at home or treat yourself at a café.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It fits neatly into the season of peppermint, eggnog, and other festive drinks.
holidays.funFact: Gingerbread is one of the oldest baked treats associated with winter celebrations. Gingerbread was baked in medieval Europe long before anyone put it in a latte.
